name: Free training programs
status: Strong Bay Area tech training is already free (for example Per Scholas, TechSF, Free City College).
use: Matched first. The grant then covers only the cost of attending: child care, transit, equipment and exam fees.

name: WIOA Individual Training Accounts
status: San Francisco's 2023 policy caps total cost at $6,000 and covers tuition and materials, not supportive services. Vouchers require a state-listed (ETPL) provider. Eligibility and current funding must be confirmed.
use: Screen residents and route them to a job center first, so the grant pays only the remainder.

name: Workforce Pell
status: Final rules took effect in July 2026 for programs of 150 to 599 clock hours. Each program needs governor and federal approval. California's status was not confirmed.
use: A future source for eligible programs at eligible institutions. Added to matching once available.

name: California CASF Adoption Account
status: $40 million authorized for FY2026-27. Recipients cannot charge for classes, and the fund does not pay rent, incentives or internet service.
use: May fund free digital foundations classes, not tuition for paid programs.

name: Federal Digital Equity Competitive Grant
status: A new notice is expected in December 2026, with final rules unknown.

name: HUD self-sufficiency programs (FSS, ROSS, Jobs-Plus)
status: The FY2027 budget request proposes no funding for FSS, ROSS or Jobs-Plus, against $206.4 million enacted for FY2026. Congress decides final funding.
use: Coordinate with existing FSS or ROSS coordinators, but do not depend on these programs.

name: Bridgeline last-dollar grant (private and local philanthropy)
status: Most flexible source. Specific funders not yet researched.
use: Primary source for the pilot grant pool, including costs public programs exclude. Paid directly to providers and vendors, never as cash.
